core_concepts: Acknowledgements On the 16th of November 1985, we took Concorde G-BOAG on a special flight to Aruba, one of our destination islands in the southern Caribbean
In a few moments, it started to rain heavily, and Concorde was framed in the most glorious of rainbows
It was then that I realised that something as beautiful as a rainbow is not made up of the simple seven colours that we all learn about as children
To my parents, Joan and Arthur, who had the courage to believe in the seven-year-old child’s dream, and to help it come true
To Nick Cook, Rowland White, Mark Lucas, Nick Lowndes, Kay Halsey, Ruth Atkins, Eloise Austin, Jen Harlow and Adrian Meredith
To all of those who spent the time to share their aviation and Concorde knowledge with me over my fifty-six years as a pilot
To the people who made Concorde the exceptional aircraft that it is
To those in my life who are no longer with us but are essential to this tale, including Maggie Bannister, Henri Perrier, Brian Trubshaw, Geoff Morell, Bob Knights and Tony Meadows
And, perhaps with the most important last, my family
I love them all dearly and literally could not have done this without them
It is made up of thousands, if not millions, of shades
It is not complete without each and every one of them
